# Changelog

## [0.3.1](https://github.com/sergenes/tilewall/releases/tag/v0.3.1) - 2026-11-16

### Better

- **Equal Tiles ends per display.** With a group on each of two displays, focusing a tile on one screen grows that tile and leaves the other screen's tiles equal. In 0.3.0 it ended on both screens at once.
- The help window describes shift drag, Equal Tiles, Always Tile and the update check.
- The repository has a changelog, generated from the release notes.

### Checked

- Two groups on two displays were tested end to end for this release: sending tiles across, each group keeping its own enlarged tile, focus cycling and reordering inside one group, shift drag inside a group and onto the other display's group, dragging and resizing one group, switching tiling off and on for one display, dropping a group on the other display, and a restart.

## [0.3.0](https://github.com/sergenes/tilewall/releases/tag/v0.3.0) - 2026-11-16

### New

- **Drag to reorder.** Hold shift while dragging a tile by its title bar. Drop it on another tile and the two trade places. Dropped on a tile of another display, it joins that group in front of that tile. Dropped anywhere else, it goes back. A drag without shift still moves the whole group.
- **Equal Tiles.** Makes every tile the same size, so nothing is enlarged. The tiles stay equal until you focus one, which then grows again. In the menu, on ctrl+alt+e, and as `tilewall even [on|off]`.

## [0.2.0](https://github.com/sergenes/tilewall/releases/tag/v0.2.0) - 2026-11-16

### New

- **Reorder tiles.** `tilewall move next` and `tilewall move prev` swap a tile with its neighbour. Also in the menu as Move Tile Forward and Move Tile Back, and on ctrl+alt+shift+d and ctrl+alt+shift+a.
- **More terminals out of the box.** A new config tiles Terminal, iTerm2, Ghostty, kitty, WezTerm, Alacritty and Warp. Only Terminal has been tested so far, so reports about the others are welcome. An existing config keeps its rules.
- **Tile any app without editing JSON.** Always Tile in the menu adds a rule for the frontmost app, and `tilewall rule add <app>` does the same from the command line.
- **Update check.** Once a day tilewall asks GitHub whether a newer release exists and shows it at the top of the menu. Nothing is downloaded. `"checkForUpdates": false` in the config switches it off, and `tilewall update` checks on request.

### Better

- **Much less idle work.** Tiling is now driven by window notifications, with a reconcile every 5 seconds instead of every second. With 14 Terminal windows, idle CPU went from about 2.2% to about 0.3% on the Mac it was measured on.
- A group dropped on a display is judged by where the pointer was during the drag.
- A command line client that hangs no longer blocks other `tilewall` commands.
- The disk image opens with the app next to the Applications folder.

## [0.1.0](https://github.com/sergenes/tilewall/releases/tag/v0.1.0) - 2026-11-13

First public release.

- Tiles the windows the rules match, Terminal by default, and grows the focused tile to a quarter of the screen.
- Landscape and portrait layouts.
- Each display has its own group, which moves and resizes like one window.
- Tiling can be switched off per display.
- Menu bar menu, hotkeys under the left hand, and a command line.
- Square window corners are experimental, see the README.
